subject.title: [Feature]: Plugin API for aborting agent runs (api.runtime.agent.abort)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a supported plugin runtime abort API, and if so what session/run ownership and permission boundary must it enforce?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but granting plugin code authority to abort runs is a new public plugin API and security-boundary decision that automation cannot infer safely.

options.title: Design a scoped plugin abort API
options.body: Approve a narrow runtime method only after defining session/run ownership checks, trusted-plugin access, SDK docs, API baseline updates, and focused Gateway/plugin runtime tests.

options.title: Use existing Gateway cancellation only
options.body: Decline a new runtime method and document `chat.abort`, `api.runtime.gateway.request`, or session cancellation as the supported boundary for operator clients and trusted runtime paths.

options.title: Defer for lifecycle API design
options.body: Keep this open but block implementation until plugin lifecycle permissions and run-management APIs are designed together.

recommendation.title: Design a scoped plugin abort API
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow runtime method only after defining session/run ownership checks, trusted-plugin access, SDK docs, API baseline updates, and focused Gateway/plugin runtime tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This needs product/security direction across Plugin SDK and Gateway surfaces, and this handle has the strongest adjacent runtime/API decision history in the inspected evidence.
